name: Black And White Marriage
overview: Scripture addresses marriage in the context of maintaining distinct boundaries between different kinds, as seen in Leviticus 19:19's prohibition against mixing diverse kinds in various areas of life. The example of Moses marrying an Ethiopian woman (Numbers 12:1) shows that interracial marriage did occur, though other passages like Deuteronomy 7:3 and Nehemiah 13:23 caution against marrying outside the covenant community. The New Testament records the marriage at Cana (John 2:1) without distinction of race, emphasizing the sanctity of marriage itself. Overall, the biblical narrative upholds marriage as a covenant relationship that reflects God's order, with careful attention to the spiritual and communal implications of marital unions.
